office_does: The auditor records deeds and documents, runs county elections, handles licensing and keeps the county's books; in San Juan County the office also prepares the county budget. Nonpartisan, four-year term.
race_blurb: The incumbent against her former chief deputy. Natasha Warmenhoven runs on her first-term record; Heather Lee, who resigned in March saying the office lacked transparency, responsiveness and consistency, promises a different approach. Neither states positions on wider policy.

candidates.summary: Former Chief Deputy Auditor (three years, through March 2026) who resigned over the office's direction; now a finance consultant to local districts and the Town of Friday Harbor.
highlights: Chief Deputy Auditor for three years; earlier Payroll Deputy and Elections Specialist [S1]
Says the office lacks "transparency, responsiveness, and consistency" and wants to rebuild morale [S1][S6]
Would work to reopen the licensing desk five days a week [S3]
Endorsed by the San Juan County Democrats and former Auditor Milene Henley [S4]

experience.basis: Has not held elected office and runs on changing the office's direction, though her case rests on three years as its second-in-command.

candidates.summary: San Juan County Auditor since 2023 and Chief Deputy Auditor from 2020, running on her first-term record: budgets, financial reporting, a new financial system and elections.
highlights: Auditor since January 2023; Chief Deputy Auditor 2020-2023; certified elections administrator [S1]
Cites balanced 2024-2025 and 2026 budgets, a Budget-in-Brief and expanded quarterly reports [S3][S4]
Leading the county's new financial management system, set for March 2027 [S3]
Her office prepared the balanced 2027 preliminary budget [S5]

experience.basis: First-term incumbent with six years in the office's top two jobs, running on 'Experience. Integrity. Stability.' and her record.
